column1: # tools/self/known-bypass-shapes.tsv — keel-self-maintenance (dir #842 B11; dir #68: never installed by install.sh).
# The sensor's shape table for the guards' known-bypass registers: one row per CLASS = one command-reading register
# entry that carries a `[bypass:<class>]` key in its register file. tools/self/bypass-scan.sh reads it; the classes live
# in the guards' accumulator (owner `guards`, threshold 2, window 90, counts felt — `bypass-scan.sh classes` prints the
# `accumulate.sh new-class` lines). An entry about a file's content or a machine state (a hook started with stdin closed,
# a test file that traps TERM, a link planted at a claimed temp path) has no transcript to scan, so it has no row here and
# carries no key (tests/test_bypass_scan.sh holds both lists).
# Columns, tab-separated (the first non-comment row is the header):
#   class      `<guard>:<shape-slug>` — the accumulator's class id and the key written in the register line.
#   register   the repo-relative file whose comment holds the entry (the key appears there exactly once).
#   pattern    an awk ERE (LC_ALL=C) tested against ONE command with its newlines turned into ` ; `. It finds CANDIDATES,
#              not bypasses: a pattern cannot tell a construction from real work, so every hit is adjudicated by the
#              session running the scan (docs/grooming.md G0). Macros, expanded before matching: {PUSH} a `git … push`,
#              {PR} a `gh pr create`, {ACT} either, {ACTAT} either at a command position (after `;`, `&`, `|`,
#              `(` or the start — a heredoc body line starts after the ` ; ` that stands for its newline).
#   actor      `any` — every Bash command; `subagent` — only a command in a subagent's transcript (isSidechain).
